label: CAS name
description:
A CAS Registry Number (CAS RN®) is a unique and unambiguous identifier for a specific substance that allows clear communication and, with the help of CAS scientists, links together all available data and research about that substance. Governmental agencies rely on CAS Registry Numbers for substance identification in regulatory applications because they are unique, easily validated, and internationally recognized.

CAS Name is the substance name associated to the CAS Number.

label: CAS Number
title: Chemical Abstracts Service Registry Number
description:
A CAS Registry Number is a unique and unambiguous identifier for a specific substance that allows clear communication and, with the help of CAS scientists, links together all available data and research about that substance. Governmental agencies rely on CAS Registry Numbers for substance identification in regulatory applications because they are unique, easy validated, and internationally recognized.

Each CAS Registry Number (CAS RN) identifier:
    Is a unique numeric identifier.
    Designates only one substance.
    Has no chemical significance.
    Is a link to a wealth of information about a specific chemical substance.
		
A CAS Registry Number is a numeric identifier that can contain up to 10 digits, divided by hyphens into three parts.
The right-most digit is a check digit used to verify the validity and uniqueness of the entire number.
For example, 58-08-2 is the CAS Registry Number for caffeine.

label: EC Number
description:
The EC-number, i.e. the EINECS, ELINCS or NLP number, is the official number of the 
substance within the European Union. The EC-number can be obtained from the official 
publications of EINECS, ELINCS and NLP and of the European Chemicals Agency.  
The EC-number consists of 7 digits of the type x1x2x3-x4x5x6-x7. The first digit is defined 
by the list to which the substance belongs.
The information which source of EC Number (EINECS, ELINCS and NLP as official number) or "List Number" (as non-offical number) is optional.

label: EU REACH-Number
description: A REACH number is an 18-digit identifier assigned by the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) to substances registered under the EU REACH regulation. This number serves as proof that a company has fulfilled its registration obligations for a particular substance

label: Index Name CLP Annex VI Tab 3
description: name of substance used in CLP Annex VI Tab 3

label: Index Number CLP Annex VI Tab 3
description:
The index number is a European Union identifier for a specific hazardous substance. The list of index numbers was originally listed in Annex I to Directive 67/548/EEC[1] and is now in Annex VI to Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP)[2]. It is regularly adapted to technical progress.

The index number must be distinguished from the EC number.
The index number of the individual substances consists of a character sequence according to the pattern ABC-RST-VW-Y.

ABC identifies the element or organic group that is most characteristic for the properties of the substance. For elements, their atomic number is used; organic substances are grouped into classes due to their diversity, with each class being assigned a number.
RST is the consecutive number of the substance in the ABC series.
VW indicates the form in which the substance is manufactured or placed on the market.
Y is the control number, which is calculated using the ten-digit ISBN method.

label: Constituent Substance Category
description: According to REACH and CLP, a substance may contain: one or more main constituents: Ingredient(s) that make up a large part of a substance and are therefore used in the designation and identification of the substance; the main ingredient(s) should be significantly different from the following two constituents. Impurities: any unintentional constituents resulting from the manufacturing process or originating from the raw material(s). These impurities may be the result of secondary or incomplete reactions during production and may be present in the final material even if the manufacturer did not intend their occurrence. Additives: all ingredients that have been added intentionally for example to maintain the stability of the substance and only for this purpose.
Description:de: Gemäß REACH und CLP kann ein Stoff Folgendes enthalten: einen oder mehrere Hauptbestandteile: Bestandteil(e), der/die einen großen Teil  eines Stoffes ausmacht/en und deshalb bei der Bezeichnung und Identifizierung des  Stoffes verwendet wird/werden; der/die Hauptbestandteil(e) sollte(n) sich deutlich von  den folgenden zwei Bestandteilen unterscheiden. Verunreinigungen: alle unbeabsichtigten Bestandteile, die aus dem Herstellungsprozess herrühren oder aus dem/den Ausgangsstoff(en) stammen. Diese Verunreinigungen können Ergebnis sekundärer oder unvollständiger Reaktionen während der Produktion sein und auch dann im Endstoff vorliegen, wenn der Hersteller ihr Vorkommen nicht beabsichtigt hat. Zusatzstoffe: alle Bestandteile, die z.B. zur Wahrung der Stabilität des Stoffes und nur dafür absichtlich zugesetzt wurden.

label: Latitude
description:
Latitude is a measurement of a location north or south of the Equator. Lines of latitude (also called parallels) are imaginary lines that circle Earth’s surface, running east and west parallel to the Equator. It is measured in degrees (°), which may be broken down into smaller units called minutes (′) and seconds (″). It can also be expressed in decimal degrees; negative values of decimal degrees represent latitudes in the Southern Hemisphere and longitudes in the Western Hemisphere.
Lines of latitude north of the Equator (the line that marks 0° latitude) are numbered from 1° to 89° N, and those south of the Equator are numbered from 1° to 89° S."

Granularity with 5 decimals is approx. to 1 meter.

Can be displayed as a decimal number 30.14402˚ , -30.14402 or 30.14402˚ N, 30.14402 N or with degrees minutes and seconds 30˚ 2‘ 12’ N or 30˚ 5‘ 34.113’ S or in  a short form  4626N (degrees, minutes, N/S)
Description:de:
Der Breitengrad ist ein Maß für einen Ort nördlich oder südlich des Äquators. Breitengradlinien (auch Parallelen genannt) sind imaginäre Linien, die die Erdoberfläche umkreisen und parallel zum Äquator nach Osten und Westen verlaufen. Er wird in Grad (°) gemessen, die in kleinere Einheiten, die Minuten (′) und Sekunden (″), unterteilt werden können. Er kann auch in Dezimalgraden ausgedrückt werden; negative Werte von Dezimalgraden stehen für Breitengrade in der südlichen Hemisphäre und für Längengrade in der westlichen Hemisphäre.
Die Breitengrade nördlich des Äquators (die Linie, die den 0. Breitengrad markiert) sind von 1° bis 89° N nummeriert, die südlich des Äquators von 1° bis 89° S.“

Die Granularität mit 5 Dezimalstellen entspricht ca. 1 Meter.

Kann als Dezimalzahl 30.14402˚ , -30.14402 oder 30.14402˚ N, 30.14402 N oder mit Grad Minuten und Sekunden 30˚ 2' 12' N oder 30˚ 5' 34.113' S angezeigt werden.

label: Longitude
description:
Lines of longitude (also called meridians) run between the geographic North Pole and the geographic South Pole and are used to measure distances from the prime meridian. It is measured in degrees (°), which may be broken down into smaller units called minutes (′) and seconds (″). It can also be expressed in decimal degrees; negative values of decimal degrees represent latitudes in the Southern Hemisphere and longitudes in the Western Hemisphere. Lines of longitude east of the prime meridian (the line that marks 0° longitude) are numbered from 1° to 179° east (E). Lines of longitude west of the prime meridian are numbered from 1° to 179° west (W).

5 decimals result in a granularity of approx. 1 meter.

Can be displayed as a decimal number 30.14402˚ , -30.14402 or 30.14402˚ W, -30.14402 E or with degrees minutes and seconds 30˚ 2‘ 12’ W or 30˚ 5‘ 34.113’ E or in a short form  00612E (degree, minutes, W/E)
Description:de:
Die Längengrade (auch Meridiane genannt) verlaufen zwischen dem geografischen Nordpol und dem geografischen Südpol und werden zur Messung von Entfernungen vom Nullmeridian verwendet. Er wird in Grad (°) gemessen, die in kleinere Einheiten, die Minuten (′) und Sekunden (″), unterteilt werden können. Er kann auch in Dezimalgraden ausgedrückt werden; negative Werte von Dezimalgraden stehen für Breitengrade auf der Südhalbkugel und für Längengrade auf der Westhalbkugel. Die Längengrade östlich des Nullmeridians (die Linie, die den 0. Längengrad markiert) sind von 1° bis 179° Ost (E) nummeriert. Die Längengrade westlich des Nullmeridians sind von 1° bis 179° West (W) nummeriert.

5 Dezimalstellen ergeben eine Granularität von ca. 1 Meter.

Kann als Dezimalzahl 30.14402˚ , -30.14402 oder 30.14402˚ W, -30.14402 E oder mit Grad, Minuten und Sekunden angezeigt werden 30˚ 2' 12' W oder 30˚ 5' 34.113' E

label: GWP Aviation emissions (production gate to customer gate if applicable)
description: Position H: Aviation emissions occurring in the reported distrubution stage after the production gate until customer gate (if applicable).\n

label: GWP fossil
description: Position A: includes all fossil emissions, including industrial processes, stationary/mobile combustion and fugitive emissions. This position inlcudes the fossil emissions associated to land management (A1: "GWP fossil lanf management")\n

label: GWP fossil land management
description: Position A1: fossil emissions occurring in land management activities. This is a detailed, which must be included in the total position A "GWP fossil". It encompasses emissions as described in PACT v3.0: N2O emissions from fertilizers; fossil CO2 emissions from soil management; CO2 emissions from soil amendments (such as lime, urea and other inputs); land management production emissions (including CO2 emissions from on-site machinery, and emissions from manufacturing of production inputs such as fertilizers and chemical inputs,); hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) and perfluorocarbons (PFCs) emissions from air-conditioning and refrigerant use; emissions from on-site waste or wastewater management; indirect emissions from purchased energy associated with land management production activities.\n

label: GWP Land Management CO2 Emissions
description: Position F: carbon stock losses occurring within the same land use category or subcategory due to agricultural practices such as tillage, field preparations, pruning and harvest. Land Management CO2 emissions measures biogenic CO2 emissions from a net loss in carbon stock within one land use category or subcategory. This includes impact on the land-carbon pools,including above- and below-ground biomass, dead organic matter, and soil carbon pools. If the carbon stock increases within the same land use category and the conditions to report removals are met, this may be calculated as a Land management CO2 removal (position G). Refer to PACT v3.0 for details.\n

label: GWP Land Management CO2 Removals
description: Position G (negative contribution): Land management removals are net CO2 removals resulting from net increases to carbon stored in land-based carbon pools (biomass, dead organic matter and soil carbon pools) due to ongoing land management practices. This extra net carbon stock is gained over the crop rotation or crop cultivation cycle (e.g., multiple years for perennial crops and multiple years in a rotation that includes annual crops). Refer to PACT v3.0 for details.\n

label: GWP land use change (LUC, excluding iLUC)
description: Position E: Emissions from LUC constitute a release of GHG emissions due to a change in land use from one land use category or subcategory to another, such as primary forest to agricultural land, or peat land (type of wetland) to cropland. This position encompasses dLUC (direct land use change) emissions. If that data is not available, companies should account for LUC using statistical land-use change (sLUC) emissions. iLUC emissions are excluded. Refer to PACT v3.0 for details. \n

label: GWP Removals (BECCS)
description: Position B (negative contribution): carbon capture and geologic storage of CO2 emissions and counting as removal (e.g. technology capture of biogenic CO2 emissions / BECCS - refer to PACT v3.0). Apply mandatorily only if in "CCS/BECCS applied" the option "True" has been selected, AND only if the case of "removal" (e.g. BECCS) applies. If it's not a removal, the field should be declared as "0".\n

label: comment
description:
Any additional information related to the PCF. Whereas the property productDescription 
contains product-level information, comment should be used for information and instructions 
related to the calculation of the PCF, or other information which informs the ability to interpret
(e.g. LUC not included as unable to calculate LUC), to audit, or to verify the PCF.


Information explaining the current status of the PCF, what was changed since the last version, etc. If the PCF was changed since a previous version, indicate all methodological and/or production process change(s) that occurred to result in the PCF change. For example, include the relevant change(s) from the list below:

1. In case product or sector specific guidance used does not align with PACT Methodology's requirement, the areas of disalignment should be specified in the comment section (e.g. allocation rules, exemption rules, data quality metrics).

2. Information explaining the current status of the PCF, what was changed since the last version, etc. If the PCF was changed since a previous version, indicate all methodological and/or production process change(s) that occurred to result in the PCF change. E.g., include the relevant change(s) from the list below: 

Methodological:
 - Access to new Emission Factor data (database, supplier-specific, company-specific)
 - Updated upstream data (i.e. upstream supplier updated their PCF based on methodology change)

Production Process:
 - Change in process
 - Change in feedstock
 - Change from conventional to certified sustainable material
 - Change in energy source
 - Change in upstream supplier
 - Updated upstream data (i.e. upstream supplier updated their PCF based on process change)

 3. Additional information on biogenic emissions & removals calculation  should be specified. This includes information on tools used for  calculations (e.g. Cool Farm Tool), and methodological choices made in calculation of biogenic emissions and removals (e.g. Statistical  or Direct Land use change calculation for DLUC calculations).

label: crossSectoralStandards
description:
The cross-sectoral standards applied for calculating or allocating [=GHG=] emissions.

It MUST be a non-empty array and SHOULD contain only the following values without duplicates:

  : `ISO14067`
  :: for the ISO 14067 Standard, "Greenhouse gases â€” Carbon footprint of products â€” Requirements and guidelines for quantification"
  : `ISO14083`
  :: for the ISO 14083 Standard, "Greenhouse gases â€” Quantification and reporting of greenhouse gas emissions arising from transport chain operations"
  : `ISO14040-44`
  :: for the ISO 14040-44 Standard, "Environmental management â€” Life cycle assessment â€” Principles and framework"
  : `GHGP-Product`
  :: for the Greehouse Gas Protocol (GHGP) Product Standard
  : `PEF`
  :: for the EU Product Environmental Footprint Guide
  : `PACT-1.0`
  : `PACT-2.0`
  : `PACT-3.0`
  :: for a given version of the [=PACT Methodology=]. It is recommended to use the latest version of the Methodology.
  : `PAS2050`
  :: for the Publicly Available Specification (PAS) 2050, "Specification for the assessment of the life cycle greenhouse gas emissions of goods and services". The use of this standard is permitted but not recommended.

The enumeration of standards above CAN evolve in future revisions. A host system MUST accept ProductFootprints from later revisions with `crossSectoralStandards` containing values that are not defined in this specification.

and boundary of the product carbon footprint.

label: EINECS
title: Official EC Number
description: EINECS (European Inventory of Existing Commercial Chemical Substances) is an inventory of substances that deemed to be on the European Community market between 1 January 1971 and 18 September 1981. EINECS also indicates CAS number, EC number, substance name and its molecular formula. Chemicals listed in the EINECS are considered phase-in substances under the REACH Regulation.

label: ELINCS
title: Official EC Number
description: ELINCS (European List of Notified Chemical Substances) in support of the 7th amendment to Directive 67/548/EEC. ELINCS lists those substances which were notified under Directive 67/548/EEC, the Dangerous Substances Directive Notification of New Substances (NONS) that became commercially available after 18 September 1981.

label: List Number
title: Non official List Number
description:
List numbers are technical identifiers that do not have any legal significance, but might be useful for identifying substances especially when no other numerical identifier is present. They are issued by the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA).
Format: NNN-NNN-R, where the N represents alphanumerical characters and R is a check digit

label: NLP
title: Official EC Number
description: NLP (No-Longer Polymers). The definition of polymers was changed in April 1992 by Council Directive 92/32/EEC amending Directive 67/548/EEC, with the result of that substances previously considered to be polymers were no longer excluded from REACH Regulation. The NLP list was drawn up, consisting of such substance that were commercially available between 18 September 1981 and 31 October 1993.

label: Latitude
description:
"Latitude is a measurement of a location north or south of the Equator. Lines of latitude (also called parallels) are imaginary lines that circle Earth’s surface, running east and west parallel to the Equator. It is measured in degrees (°), which may be broken down into smaller units called minutes (′) and seconds (″). It can also be expressed in decimal degrees; negative values of decimal degrees represent latitudes in the Southern Hemisphere and longitudes in the Western Hemisphere.
Lines of latitude north of the Equator (the line that marks 0° latitude) are numbered from 1° to 89° N, and those south of the Equator are numbered from 1° to 89° S."

label: Longitude
description: Lines of longitude (also called meridians) run between the geographic North Pole and the geographic South Pole and are used to measure distances from the prime meridian. It is measured in degrees (°), which may be broken down into smaller units called minutes (′) and seconds (″). It can also be expressed in decimal degrees; negative values of decimal degrees represent latitudes in the Southern Hemisphere and longitudes in the Western Hemisphere. Lines of longitude east of the prime meridian (the line that marks 0° longitude) are numbered from 1° to 179° east (E). Lines of longitude west of the prime meridian are numbered from 1° to 179° west (W).

label: GWP Aviation emissions (production gate to customer gate if applicable)
description: Position H: Aviation emissions occurring in the reported distrubution stage after the production gate until customer gate (if applicable).\n

label: GWP biogenic CO2-uptake (biogenic CO2 contained in the product)
description: Position D (negative contributuion): biogenic CO2 uptake in the product. It can be attributed by means of Mass Balancing: in such a case the "Mass Balancing used" must be set to "True". Apply mandatorily if in "Biogenic Carbon Content" a non-"0" has been selected.\n

label: GWP biogenic emissions other than CO2
description:
Position C: non-CO2 biogenic emissions related to agricultural activities. It encompasses emissions as described in PACT v3.0: CH4 emissions from livestock and manure; CH4 emissions from biomass burning and fires; 
CH4 emissions from rice production; CH4 emissions from transformation and degradation (e.g., combustion, digestion, composting, landfilling). It must be noted that N2O from land management activities are not included in this position and are reported in position A and A1 (as a detail).\n

label: GWP fossil
description: Position A: includes all fossil emissions, including industrial processes, stationary/mobile combustion and fugitive emissions. This position inlcudes the fossil emissions associated to land management (A1: "GWP fossil lanf management")\n

label: GWP fossil land management
description: Position A1: fossil emissions occurring in land management activities. This is a detailed, which must be included in the total position A "GWP fossil". It encompasses emissions as described in PACT v3.0: N2O emissions from fertilizers; fossil CO2 emissions from soil management; CO2 emissions from soil amendments (such as lime, urea and other inputs); land management production emissions (including CO2 emissions from on-site machinery, and emissions from manufacturing of production inputs such as fertilizers and chemical inputs,); hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) and perfluorocarbons (PFCs) emissions from air-conditioning and refrigerant use; emissions from on-site waste or wastewater management; indirect emissions from purchased energy associated with land management production activities.\n

label: GWP Land Management CO2 Emissions
description: Position F: carbon stock losses occurring within the same land use category or subcategory due to agricultural practices such as tillage, field preparations, pruning and harvest. Land Management CO2 emissions measures biogenic CO2 emissions from a net loss in carbon stock within one land use category or subcategory. This includes impact on the land-carbon pools,including above- and below-ground biomass, dead organic matter, and soil carbon pools. If the carbon stock increases within the same land use category and the conditions to report removals are met, this may be calculated as a Land management CO2 removal (position G). Refer to PACT v3.0 for details.\n

label: GWP Land Management CO2 Removals
description: Position G (negative contribution): Land management removals are net CO2 removals resulting from net increases to carbon stored in land-based carbon pools (biomass, dead organic matter and soil carbon pools) due to ongoing land management practices. This extra net carbon stock is gained over the crop rotation or crop cultivation cycle (e.g., multiple years for perennial crops and multiple years in a rotation that includes annual crops). Refer to PACT v3.0 for details.\n

label: GWP land use change (LUC, excluding iLUC)
description: Position E: Emissions from LUC constitute a release of GHG emissions due to a change in land use from one land use category or subcategory to another, such as primary forest to agricultural land, or peat land (type of wetland) to cropland. This position encompasses dLUC (direct land use change) emissions. If that data is not available, companies should account for LUC using statistical land-use change (sLUC) emissions. iLUC emissions are excluded. Refer to PACT v3.0 for details. \n

label: GWP Removals (BECCS)
description: Position B (negative contribution): carbon capture and geologic storage of CO2 emissions and counting as removal (e.g. technology capture of biogenic CO2 emissions / BECCS - refer to PACT v3.0). Apply mandatorily only if in "CCS/BECCS applied" the option "True" has been selected, AND only if the case of "removal" (e.g. BECCS) applies. If it's not a removal, the field should be declared as "0".\n

label: Hazard pictogram code
description:
EU CLP sets detailed criteria for the labelling elements: pictograms, signal words and standard statements for hazard, prevention, response, storage and disposal, for every hazard class and category.

A hazard pictogram is an image on a label that includes a warning symbol and specific colours intended to provide information about the damage a particular substance or mixture can cause to our health or the environment. The pictograms are those applied in the United Nations Globally Harmonised System (UN GHS).

label: Precautionary Statement Code - Disposal
description:
EU P-Phrases (Precautionary Statements) are standardized, legally binding safety measures under the CLP Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008. They instruct users on handling hazardous chemicals safely to minimize risks. These phrases are categorized into general, prevention, response, storage, and disposal advice, replacing the old S-phrases.

Precautionary Statements for Hazardous Substances and Mixtures - Standardised safety advice for the label. For labels only the description will be used.

description: The unique identifier of the manufacturer

label: Date of issue
description: The time stamp at which the Circularity Content (e.g., Recycled, Renewable), has been declared, independently of when or if it has been shared. This represents the validity period start unless specified seperately.

label: Reference period end
description: End of time period of data collection for primary data sources

label: Reference period start
description: Start of time period of data collection for primary data sources (this does not refer to publication dates of secondary data)

label: Validity period end
description: Time stamp declaring the expected end of the use period for this declaration or date of expected update (i.e. when does the data validity period end?).
DefaultValue: Resolving attribute: 3 years after "reference period start"

label: Danger
title: Signal word for severe hazard categories
description: Signal word "DANGER" for severe hazard categories

label: Warning
title: Signal word for less severe hazard categories
description: Signal word "WARNING" for less severe hazard categories

label: "Classified according CLP"?
description: Is a substance "classified according CLP" (boolean=yes) all substance hazard information shall be delivered. Is a substance "not classifiued" hazard information could be deliverd.

label: CLP Annex VI Notes
hasRange: /IM Enumerations/CLP Annex VI code and notes
description: The CLP Annex VI Notes provides guidelines for the harmonized classification and labeling of hazardous substances (Special conditions for classification of listed substance)

label: CLP ATE
description: Acute toxicity Estimates published in CLP Annex VI table 3 or part of self-classification

label: CLP M-Factor Aquatic Acute
description:
M-factor stands for multiplying factor for substances that are highly toxic to aquatic environment (i.e, LC50 or EC50<1mg/L).
The purpose of applying an M-factor is to give an increased weight to highly toxic components when classifying a mixture. Values are in continued factor 10 intervals without an unit.

label: CLP M-Factor Aquatic Chronic
description:
M-factor stands for multiplying factor for substances that are highly toxic to aquatic environment (i.e, LC50 or EC50<1mg/L).
The purpose of applying an M-factor is to give an increased weight to highly toxic components when classifying a mixture. Values are in continued factor 10 intervals without an unit.

label: CLP  specific concentration limits
title: SCL
description: If substance has a SCL published in CLP it is triggering a hazard classification if present in a certain percentage.

label: Hazard Class, Category Code and Statement
description: Hazard Class and Catergory Code as in CLP/Reach defined following OECD guidelines

label: Listed in CLP Annex VI
description: Official harmonized classification in Annex VI of CLP.

label: CAS Name
description: The name of a substance associated with the CAS registry number

label: CAS number
description: A CAS Registry Number (CAS RN®) is a unique and unambiguous identifier for a specific substance that allows clear communication and, with the help of CAS scientists, links together all available data and research about that substance. Governmental agencies rely on CAS Registry Numbers for substance identification in regulatory applications because they are unique, easily validated, and internationally recognized.

label: CLP Annex VI Chemical name
hasRange: Index Name CLP Annex VI Tab 3
description: Name of substance used in the CLP Annex VI

label: CLP Annex VI index number (Index No)
hasRange: Index Number CLP Annex VI Tab 3
description: A reference number for a substance within the Classification and Labelling (C&L) Inventory, which details its hazardous properties and required labeling under the CLP Regulation (Classification, Labelling and Packaging).

label: EC Number
description: The EC-number, i.e. the EINECS, ELINCS or NLP number, is the official number of the substance within the European Union. The EC-number can be obtained from the official publications of EINECS, ELINCS and NLP and of the European Chemicals Agency.

label: EU REACH registration number
description:
The European Chemicals Agency shall assign a submission number to each registration, which is to be used for
all correspondence regarding the registration until the registration is deemed to be
complete.

label: INCI
description: INCI names (International Nomenclature Cosmetic Ingredient) are systematic names internationally recognized to identify cosmetic ingredients.

label: IUPAC Name
description: IUPAC Nomenclature ensures that each compound (and its various isomers) have only one formally accepted name known as the systematic IUPAC name.

label: Substance name as REACH registered
description: Name used for registration purposes according to REACH

label: Trivial name
description: Retained names are often used for the most fundamental parts of a nomenclature system: almost all the chemical elements have retained names rather than being named systematically, as do the first four alkanes, benzene and most simple heterocyclic compounds. Water and ammonia are other examples of retained names.

Or a measuring condition  is given: 
Temperature and/or pressure
